Confusion metrics for edge selection at a threshold

Source: R/eval.R
confusion_at_threshold.Rd

Compares a score matrix (e.g. posterior inclusion probabilities) with a true adjacency matrix. An edge is predicted when its score is >= threshold. A 0/1 (or logical) estimated adjacency matrix can be passed as score_mat with the default threshold.

Usage

confusion_at_threshold(
  score_mat,
  truth_mat,
  threshold = 0.5,
  upper_only = TRUE
)

Arguments

score_mat

Numeric p x p matrix of edge scores, or a vector of edge scores (e.g. an upper triangle) of the same length as truth_mat.

truth_mat

p x p matrix of true edges (non-zero = edge), or a vector matching score_mat.

threshold

Numeric threshold. Default 0.5.

upper_only

Logical. If TRUE (default), only the upper triangle is used (each undirected edge once); otherwise all off-diagonal entries. Ignored for vectors.

Value

A list with TP, FP, TN, FN, TPR (sensitivity, power), FPR, precision, F1, FDR (1 - precision) and MCC (Matthews correlation coefficient). Rates whose denominator is zero are NA; in particular FDR is NA when no edge is predicted and MCC is NA when any margin of the confusion table is 0.

Details

Edges with a missing score or truth are dropped.

Examples

truth <- matrix(c(0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0), 3, 3)
score <- matrix(c(0, .9, .6, .9, 0, .2, .6, .2, 0), 3, 3)
confusion_at_threshold(score, truth, threshold = 0.5)
#> $TP
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $FP
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $TN
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $FN
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $TPR
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#> $FPR
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $precision
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#> $F1
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#> $FDR
#> [1] 0.5
#> 
#> $MCC
#> [1] -0.5
#> 

# A 0/1 estimated adjacency matrix
confusion_at_threshold(threshold_to_adjacency(score, 0.5), truth)$MCC
#> [1] -0.5
